author: Kelli Volk
title: AG: DOC inmate's death a suspected overdose - NewsBreak
text:
By Kelli Volk ,
1 hours ago
SIOUX FALLS, S.D. (KELO) — The death of a 33-year-old South Dakota prison inmate could be the result of a drug overdose.
The DOC says Travis Long Fox was found unresponsive in his cell at the state penitentiary last Tuesday.
He was taken to a hospital where he died Friday.
The state’s top prosecutor, Marty Jackley, says Fox’s death is being investigated as a suspected overdose.
When asked how Fox may have accessed a drug, Jackley said there’s an ongoing investigation.
“We are running down all the leads we have obtained. We feel good about this investigation. Obviously it’s a tragedy anytime there’s a death in the penitentiary, but we’re taking it as serious as we always do, these cases in the penitentiary. And we will continue this investigation until we reach a point where the evidence supports a criminal charge,” Jackley said.
The DCI has investigated five suspected overdose deaths of DOC inmates in Sioux Falls since February.
“Two of those inmate cases have resulted in criminal indictments and are set for a jury trial in January,” Jackley said.
The issue could be up for discussion in the legislature next year.
“As attorney general, I’ve taken a no tolerance to drugs in the penitentiary. I suspect this session I’ll be working with legislators to enhance our statutes to prevent distribution and ingestion in the walls of the penitentiary,” Jackley said.
Jackley says the five deaths aren’t the only instances where investigators have found drugs in the penitentiary.
He says the most common drugs investigators see are methamphetamine and K-2.
